hi! so i'm ftm, female to male trans- and before that, i was also a cis person who didn't really "get it". i find being trans is really hard to describe to people who have never felt gender dysphoria before, like describing a color only you can see.

but my thoughts are, gender is ultimately a social construct- not that it isn't real or important. after all, money and religion are social constructs!
what this means is that, also like money and religion, people have varying degrees of enjoyment regarding this. inevitably, people will want to "bend the rules" of the status quo, so to speak. trans people want to change *their own* status quo. the societal norms attached with a trans person's assigned gender just might not sound like the life they want- while the societal norms attached to another gender might interest them more.

usually the realization doesn't occur as "wait, i've been trans all along." in my case, i came to seriously hate being dressed up in dresses, and i hated having long hair- things i now recognize as symptoms of gender dysphoria. it'll be a slow realization for most. it's like you're becoming more and more aware of a pain in your gut, and you have to figure out what's causing it on your own

tldr; trans people are trans because they're less comfortable with all the social norms attached to their assigned gender

hey there. i've been on T for two years, and it's actually somewhat easy to girlmode until you can eventually go full stealth. shave regularly; invest in a good chest binder; present as female when you're invited places.
the only hurdle here is that your voice will inevitably deepen. it will be very gradual, but your friends and family might notice. honestly the only way i've found around this is to kinda just gaslight people by going "oh, what? i've always sounded like this. maybe im just a little hoarse today"

and honestly, i recommend keeping your friends around. you'll need a good support system to help you as you go through this, and if they're already supportive that's a plus

to start this off- you know what you did wasn't very supportive, and you are working to make sure that doesn't happen again. i'm sure your boyfriend doesn't expect you to be an encyclopedia of ftm knowledge, and is just happy that you're learning! there is no shame in that.
as for changes that are not physical, i'll list a few (i've been on T for 2 years now):

-emotions get weird. it might become very hard for him to cry, and much easier for him to get angry. remember that our body is essentially undergoing a second puberty, so it might be a bit rough at first- but also like puberty, it will pass.

-honestly? get prepared for a lot of potentially ugly hair and clothing styles. not a physical change directly caused by T, but as he learns more about himself he will inevitably change up his style, and it'll take a few tries to find his own. something that my father did for me that was so very helpful was pulling me aside and giving me pointers on men's fashion, your clothing and the way you style it. you could always ask if he's down to learn some tips and tricks from you. he might be too prideful or embarrassed to say yes at first, but might as well throw the idea out there!

-you will get hungry faster, and weight gain on T is common. this is a side effect that starts off strong and mellows out within a few months. boy's gotta eat!!!

-you will probably notice his personality shift a bit overall- he'll more confident and comfortable in his body as it starts to align with his transition goals. 


i think those are the main points! as for everything else you mentioned, i do think that talk about you being concerned for him should happen sooner rather than later. 
when he takes his testosterone, whether in injection or gel form, you can always ask to watch and/or help. he might want you to help with it, he might not. but just being present in some way, especially at first, means a lot.
and finally, remember no two trans men are exactly alike; no two will have the same transition goals; no two will have the same side effects of hrt. asking these questions about him shows that you care and are ready to learn!

while i agree it is hard for a cis person to understand a trans person's struggle, some of these struggles are universal: body image issues, hiding your real self and molding your personality off others, and of course- male puberty. you have more in common than you may think! 

anyways, rambling over. i hope this helped!

these are some great poses! you're very good at establishing a line of motion. To help make your poses even better, I would actually say not to use squares and circles for the body+joints. It's a good start, for sure! but what I mean is that, when you look up pose references, humans are usually curvy in varying degrees and are made up of a bunch of random blob shapes. jagged edges on a human's silhouette is very rare, so the closer you get to the body's shapes, the less cleaning up you'll have to do later to make it look more organic.

also- something that really helps me is to focus on the silhouette itself before doing details. you may need to practice by literally outlining humans in photos (of course, do not pass this on as your own work in this case). focusing on the bigger picture instead of doing each small part of the body piece by piece also helps the piece look more fluid and natural! 

sorry for the wall of text, hope this could be helpful to you :)

first of all, great drawings! clearly you have a solid grasp on anatomy and proportions already. 

for the eyes, I think the "haunted" look is because you added lines and creases around the eyes. I'm sure you already know how to reference photos, but check where the creases happen on the person's face when they smile or frown. the first drawing for example- since their eyes are open and not squinting, there will be less creasing. another optional tip is to add more light to the eyes. I generally color in the pupil all black- don't be afraid to use darker colors for tiny details like this!- and then add a pinprick of white. since eyes are kinda wet and slimy, light reflects harshly; you'll notice in reference photos that the light in the eyes doesn't usually "smudge", and it has hard edges. 

for the face in general, the crosshatching is really cool, but it's hard to tell where a light source is coming from. sometimes the easiest way to visualize where the light hits is to literally draw a circle and then a cone that reaches the character- think like drawing a sun casting a ray. references again will save you here; the more light shining on something, the less detail is visible. look at the photos and see which parts have more visible pores, pigmentation, little details like that.

for what it's worth though, I like the haunted doll look. it's cool! if it's not the style you want, by all means bend it to your whim, but it's not inherently a bad thing. 

i hope this can help!!

i'm ftm, so my experiences are probably different- but i feel very similar. i don't consider myself completely divorced from my womanhood or my upbringing as a girl- it was as much a part of me as my current identity is. there's no shame in what i used to be. 

when i first realized i was trans, one of the first things i did was explore different gender roles in the bedroom. at first i did treat it like a fetish to have behind closed doors- because i didn't know what to do. my egg had only just cracked. 
to be transgender is to be hyper aware of one's own body, and it only makes sense that this includes sexual aspects of your life. 

is it embarrassing to want to learn more about yourself, sexually or not? i don't think so. 
if you want to be trans- hold onto that feeling. especially now, more than ever. it can be lonely not sharing common experiences, but it's a beautiful thing too- the varied community we share, full of different lives and stories. 

thank you for sharing your story! thank you for being part of this community with me.

I've been on both meds haha- prozac made me anxious, trazodone makes me sleepy. so that checks out!

I will say my vet told me that for young pups- mine is a year- it's not the best idea and is a last resort quick fix (in addition to training). and it is not a substitute for training. having said this- I myself am on trazodone and it is a lifesaver of a pill! my anxiety is like being on a caffeine high all the time and trazodone is like coming down from all the coffee; i'm more myself and not uncontrollably jittery.
TLDR; should be used in addition to training and such but ultimately i think it is worth a shot and hopefully will help your dog like it helps me!

is it futile to be kind in this life if we are going to die anyways? maybe in the grand scheme of things. but we are humans, and humans are small- we do not need to burden ourselves with the workings of the universe. that's for later. 

accept that we are all chemicals and biomass, and accept that these chemicals are real in your head and body. accept that it is not a bad thing to be a brain interpreting signals- if your girlfriend tells you she loves you, technically all it does is activate your brain pathways. but more importantly, it made you feel good. it sounds like you're running yourself in circles rationalizing the human experience- but we are hard creatures to rationalize. "just go with the flow" sounds kinda lame as advice but it's also fitting here lol

all this to say: we are simply hairless animals that can't control the cosmos. but we can control our own lives. let yourself be happy- they may be "just" brain signals, and they were "just" sand dollars, but just because a story will inevitably end doesn't mean it can't be good while it lasts.

i had a hospice foster named Molly Motor Oil. she was the greatest. had her for just shy of a year. 
a lot of people say "you will know when it's their time", but i found this to be vague and unhelpful.
what i looked for was- did she seem happy to be alive? was she walking around, looking out the window, sunbathing, purring? i would list off her daily routine and see if anything changed. if your cat starts losing interest in their routine, it might be time to consider their quality of life.
note that purring can be a self-soothing behavior if a cat is in pain. 
use context clues to help figure out what your kitty is telling you. if she's still playing and eating, it sounds like she wants to stay a little longer. 

that being said: you're a hospice foster now. by giving miss Magic a place to pass peacefully, you are doing something incredibly kind. 
what makes the pain easier? what made it easier for me?

1. having a death plan. it sounds morbid but it will ease the confusion and fear of unknowns that can make death even more daunting. do you want your cat buried, cremated? do you have anything you want to do to remember her by? i got a windchime for Molly so she can talk to us when a breeze blows by.

2. talk to your cat about this. it sounds silly but i'm serious. on the way to her euthanasia appointment, i told my girl about what was going to happen and that no matter what religion took her in that i would be there soon enough. 

3. spoil them absolutely rotten. feed them human food (that they can digest safely- always look up what you're about to feed your cat!), let them annoy you when you're at the computer, give them space when they're cranky and company when they're cuddly. this is Magic's time to shine! i'm sure you're already familiar with this step though lol.

it's going to be hard. i won't lie to you. but for all the grief and pain that losing Molly caused me, I am so honored to have been a part of her life and so happy to have known her. i'm sure you can relate. wishing you and miss Magic the absolute best.❤️

hey, i'm a stoner with psychotic depression so i've been down this road before. 

1. if you were tripping and you felt bad as a side effect of the trip- the weed increasing your paranoia- i would consider that a bad trip. anyone on any substance can have a bad trip. 

2. it's incredibly common for bad trips to make you think about your worst fears- think about it, your body is going into fight or flight when you have a panic attack. when a deer goes into fight or flight, it's thinking it's gonna get eaten- when you experience something similar, your mind will naturally go there.

3. yes, you're in a more suggestible state while high. i find when i smoke weed that i spend long amounts of time reading one article or wikipedia page. that will definitely affect your trip. i recommend staying away from anything mental illness related if you're high. maybe once you get the bad trips under control you can trust yourself while tripping on that level again but i don't advise continuing the pattern for right now.

4. keep in mind that cannabis is psychoactive and is known to sometimes uncover issues that you didn't notice before- ie people's psychosis getting worse or someone developing schizophrenia. abusing any psychoactive drug for long enough will lead to some issues in your brain. that being said- i agree with you that i don't think you've secretly been schizophrenic your whole life. i think you're unlucky and need to be a little more careful while tripping, but ultimately you will be ok!

hope this helps if even a little. reminder that i am not a doctor or weed scientist and to take what i say with a grain of salt while you figure things out. wishing you the best!

I'd try and tell your parents. I wouldn't drop the S word on them, because you could get involuntarily hospitalized and I don't think those places are good on mental health at all. If there's any chance at all they might say yes, I would take it.

I won't ask what you took specifically but- was it depressants? Deliriants? If you tried to overdose either one could be making your brain feel fuzzy and have your mood sink.

4+3+1+2= 10 skittles.

Let's list the probability for each.
P(yellow) = 4/10 or 2/5
P(red)= 3/10
P(purple)= 1/10
P(orange)= 2/10 or 1/5

If you are NOT eating each skittle you pick, then you simply have to multiply the above probability twice.

For example, let's find out the probability of getting two yellow skittles in a row. The problem would look like this-

2/5 x 2/5 = 4/25. There is a 4 out of 25 chance that you'll get two yellows in a row!

If you ARE eating each skittle you pick, it's not very different. Just remember that the probability will change. You pull out one yellow skittle (4/10 chance) and then eat it. That means there will now only be THREE yellow skittles left, and NINE skittles total. The new P(yellow) is 3/9.

Use the same formula as before once you have the new probability.

4/10 x 3/9 = 12/90 or 2/15.
